language model: A model that looks at the text so far and gives a probability to every possible next token. Run in a loop, it writes.
end marker: An extra symbol in the dictionary that means the text stops here. When the model samples it, the name is finished.
held-out names: Names set aside before training and never trained on, used to test the model on names it has not seen.
bigram: A language model that predicts the next symbol from only the one symbol before it, using a table of counts.
perplexity: A loss turned into a number of choices by taking e to the power of the loss. A perplexity of 9 means the model is as unsure as if it were picking among 9 equally likely options.
